items.title: 日产携手英国Wayve开发自动驾驶技术
items.raw_excerpt: 日产汽车公司10日宣布，为提升正在自主研发的辅助驾驶系统“ProPILOT”下一代版本的功能，将与打造使用人工智能（AI）的自动驾驶技术的英国初创企业Wayve Technologies开展合作。目标是在城市道路及高速公路实现无需手扶方向盘的驾驶。日产计划在2027年度以后的新车上搭载该系统。首先在日本推出，随后扩展至北美等海外市场。（财联社）

excerpt_i18n.en: On the 10th, Nissan Motor Company announced a collaboration with the UK startup Wayve Technologies, which specializes in AI-based autonomous driving technology, to enhance the functionality of the next-generation version of its self-developed driver-assistance system "ProPILOT." The goal is to achieve hands-free driving on both urban roads and highways. Nissan plans to install this system in new vehicles starting from the 2027 fiscal year, initially launching in Japan and subsequently expanding to overseas markets such as North America. (Cailian Press)
excerpt_i18n.es: Nissan Motor anunció el día 10 que colaborará con la startup británica Wayve Technologies, especializada en tecnología de conducción autónoma basada en inteligencia artificial, para mejorar las funciones de la próxima generación de su sistema de asistencia a la conducción "ProPILOT", actualmente en desarrollo propio. News Highlights
1. Lan Zhanfei responds to kidnapping in South Africa: stripped naked, photographed, biometric data collected... not staged.
2. Major news! U.S. approves sale of Nvidia H200 to China with a 25% surcharge! China responds with just one sentence.
3. Alibaba establishes Qianwen C-end business group, including Qianwen, Quark, UC, and other services.

6. Sam's Club apologizes for "live mouse in mochi box": preliminary judgment indicates accidental intrusion by surrounding pests during placement at pickup point.
7. EU warns Musk: X must pay a €120 million fine!
8. Reports suggest Meta will release new AI model Avocado in Q1 next year, possibly not open-source.

Top Story
Lan Zhanfei responds to kidnapping in South Africa: stripped naked, photographed, biometric data collected... not staged.
On December 9, Lan Zhanfei's post about being kidnapped drew widespread attention. He stated that he was held at knifepoint by one person and two black accomplices in a five-star hotel in Cape Town, South Africa, with the incident lasting four to five hours. The kidnappers allegedly bribed airport and hotel staff to track his itinerary and attempted to force him to transfer money and apply for online loans, while collecting biometric information such as fingerprints, hair, and semen to fabricate a "rape" case and deter him from reporting to the police.
However, some netizens questioned whether it was staged. In response, Lan Zhanfei posted: I don't need the hype.
